chunks.title: Introduction
chunks.text:
High-level Introduction to Season's
Seasons is the autonomous, internet-native, tokenized liquidity system designed to facilitate the generation, distribution, and accumulation of yield through a polymer of modern DEFI mechanisms and a novel adaptation of predecessor mechanisms that leverage a combination of economic and social variables to derive, capture, and circulate value. An operator-owned protocol accessible only to the $SEAS token holder network.
Guiding Principles
Inspired by nature, Seasons applies 4 guiding principles across all product design considerations.
Resilience
Capable of withstanding any potentially critical issues without operational impacts.
Scalability
Capable of accommodating any number of users without deteriorating the user experience or system efficiency.
Permissionless
Always liquid. Non-custodial. No counterparty dependencies.
Efficiency
Reflexivity elements embedded into the core logic to ensure proportionality in system's growth sustainibly.
Assumptions
Seasons has been designed according to a multitude of "high-probability" outcomes of game-theory simulations, which indicate that in non-controlled environments (mainnet), operator behavior can veer dramatically. Assumptions apply to a supermajority (~67% or 2/3) of users, approximately 80% of the time.
Extractive Nature of Operators
Seasons assumes that the supermajority of operators will act in accordance to rational actor theory and imply constant strain on the system in order to recoup their allocation(s).
Long Time Preference
Seasons assumes that each new incoming operator shall maintain their position for no less than 90 days.
Agentic User Evolution
Seasons assumes that the very definition of a user is radically evolving with the advent of AI. Users are getting more sophisticated and, in turn, demand broader capabilities.
Infinite Vol
Seasons assumes that volatility across all assets and geographies will continue to increase; thus, more people will increasingly need more reliability and diversity in their selections.
Why Seasons
Seasons' Yield 3.0 model solves one of the yield industry's greatest conundrums: sustainability for perpetual scale. Predecessor models are beholden to deteriorating rates as a project's/platform's liquidity/size grows; laws of physics applied to finance as it relates to sourcing yield. Seasons synthesizes and extends the financial primitives of traditional yield mechanisms by embedding reflexive technical features and social factors to generate "boundless/non-linear" real yield through a transfer-fee implementation.
Moreover, heavily set in consideration around a burgeoning agentic internet economy, the Yield 3.0 system's embedded reflexivity features, digitally native form factor, and core output model (assets + distributions) unlocks scalable, progressive sustainability; becoming appealing for agentic users.
More on yield in the YIELD SYSTEM section of the documentation

chunks.title: YMS › Overview
chunks.text:
Yield Management System
Seasons' yield system is in its alpha experimentation phase, being actively modified/optimized for sustainability. While no fundamental changes are anticipated, adjustments to components like the weight balancing function, distribution model, transactional tax, etc., are likely with each progressive iteration of the product.
Overview
The YMS or Yield Management System is the orchestration layer of the SEASONS Yield 3.0 mechanism. It maps, coordinates, and sequences logical circuits across/between all three of the modules of the yield mechanism and their concurrent system components, namely Yield Accumulation and Yield Distribution.
The YMS is Seasons' "Data-Set Authority", playing a role at every critical junction in the flow of liquidity throughout the Seasons mechanism. In addition to monitoring the state of seasons in real time, detecting anomalies and deterring potential disruptions, it acts as a pseudo-oracle, ensuring consistency and continuity of operations.
Yield Accumulation
Composed of three (3) distinct modules for generating and capturing value, the yield mechanism operates from a risk-first perspective, where each independent constituent module optimizes for its preservation, providing a stable, reliable, and consistent flow of revenue based on asset retention. The modules are further complemented by a reflexive and unit accumulation component that ensures steady, persistent growth over juiced short-term returns.
Learn more about: Yield Accumlation
Yield Distribution
Referring to the transformation of proceeds into revenue that ultimately arrives in the hands of node operators, Season yield distribution is a multi-functional process consisting of harvesting proceeds from each module, consolidating them in an "acquirer," swapping for payout assets, and correctly disbursing them through a "distributor."
Learn more about: Yield Distribution
Router State Validation
Maintaining the State of Seasons Node Network (Director and Builder) requires multiple rounds of assurance checking (liveliness). Enforcing the criteria requirements and liquidity makes the YMS responsible for routing capital by ascribing which addresses are tentatively qualified for inclusion in the nearest future distribution.
Learn more about: Nodes

chunks.title: YMS › Data-Set Authority
chunks.text:
Data-Set Authority
In order for each component of the Yield 3.0 mechanism to function, an enforcement of algorithmic compliance against an irrefutable source of truth must be present. The YMS actively feeds all operational trust variables into Seasons, becoming the final directive on how much gets distributed at any given distribution, what assets are acquired for distribution, in what proportion and to where they are distributed, how the balance of the SSYM is utilized, when the YAV realizes its efforts to boost POL, and everything else formulaic in between.
Learn more about: Inlcusion Sets
F.A.Q.s
Frequently Asked Questions about the Yield Management System YMS.
Q: What is the YMS?
A: The YMS or Yield Management System is the oracle and orchestrator of the 3.0 mechanisms for cross-domain coordination.
Q: What does the YMS do?
A: Ensures state accuracy of the nodes, tracks and attributes the yield, serves the inclusion set, verifies sequences and resolves any potential halts, failures, or frictions.
Q: Is the YMS responsible for Capital Efficiency?
A: Yes, it routes capital in search of cost arbitrage.
Q: Is the YMS responsible for distributing yield?
A: Partially, it is responsible for ensuring the correct cadence of capital flow, in turn, ultimately having a direct influence on the bottom line of any upcoming distribution.
Q: Can the System operate without the YMS?
A: Partially, it is responsible for ensuring the correct cadence of capital flow, in turn, ultimately having a direct influence on the bottom line of any upcoming distribution; in the event of any unanticipated disruptions, functions can be forced in isolation.

chunks.title: Generation
chunks.text:
Accumulating Yield by Creating and Capturing Value.
Overview
The Generating component of the Seasons Yield Mechanism is a synthesis of three distinct value-producing modules. Each module possesses its own distinct profile; its own distinct source from which to derive revenue, its own return rate, volume profiles, and contribution capacities.
The methodology applied to the module's combination is skewed for consistency and sustainability in progressive growth. It assumes that there can/will be operational disruptions in any of the modules, thus treating them independently. Disruptions do not cross-contaminate other modules; on the contrary, detriments to any one of the three modules are transient, whereby virtue of design, the persistence of the other(s) will ultimately compensate and re-stabilize any regressive behavior.
By taking into account the unique rhythm, frequency, and value source, the system provides "weak synchrony," where the yield 3.0 output is always guaranteed. If/when isolated, each module provides a degree of self-sustainability, capable of ensuring a lower bound on the flow of capital.
Each of the modules is imbued with a recursive value-flow component, ensuring its consistent growth; when synthesized, they balance and complement one another, creating a compounding effect that amplifies impact.
TTT | Transactional Transfer Tax: Accumulation of proceeds by taxing all $SEAS token transactions. | → Reliability: Low
→ Return: High
→ Rate: Random | TTT
SSYM | Stakeholder Stablecoin Yield Module: Stablecoin lending pool, owned by token holders. | → Reliability: High
→ Return: Low
→ Rate: Fast | SSYM
YAV | Yield Asset Vaults: Vaults containing assets from the yield-payout basket, generating LP swap fees. | → Reliability: Moderate
→ Return: Low-Moderate
→ Rate: Consistent | YAV
The modules possess equal weight in the system. Initially, the TTT will drive most of the system's activity; however, over time, the other modules will reach equilibrium. The impact of each module varies with its contribution bandwidth, resulting in a wave-like matrix of yield weight shuffling.
Only 1 of the 3 modules — i.e., the Transactional Transfer Tax — have been activated at launch. As the protocol evolves and operational capital accumulates from economic activity relating to it, other modules will be engaged when certain milestones are achieved.
F.A.Q.s
Frequently Asked Questions about Accumulation.
Q: How does Seasons generate Yield?
A: Seasons uses a combination of three (3) distinct sources of revenue generation: TTT - a transactional taxation on the $SEAS tokens, SSYM - a stablecoin lending module, and the YAV - vaults executing DEFI strategies.
Q: How many modules does Seasons Yield 3.0 mechanism use?
A: Three; the TTT, SSYM, and YAV.
Q: How much does Each Module Generate?
A: Each module has its own profile that correlates to its capacity and bandwidth for contribution; to understand it best refer to each module's information.
Q: Are modules dependent on each other?
A: No, the modules are isolated from one another to avoid over-saturation.
Q: Do modules contribute to each other?
A: Yes, each module's individual work ultimately contributes to the Seasons network in a way that enhances other modules.

chunks.title: TTT › Overview
chunks.text:
Transactional Transfer Tax
Active
The TTT is the first module in the Seasons Yield 3.0 system by order of implementation. Going live immediately at launch, the TTT drives the majority of the output during the bootstrapping phase of the full mechanism.
Overview
Transactional Transfer Tax (TTT) is a core value-generation and accrual module of Seasons' Yield 3.0 mechanism, built from first principles of the digital-native internet economy.
The TTT logic is embedded in the $SEAS token's smart contract, imposing a fee on every buy, sell, and transfer. Accumulated fees are directly swapped into assets from the current Inclusion Set and distributed as yield to all active nodes.
Every on-chain movement of the $SEAS token — including transfers and trades on decentralized exchanges like Jupiter (https://jup.ag/tokens/7GdpaeSzvkx1a78rRkU11KstM1x8naMmMmmpWQnQSEAS) — invokes the transactional tax (txTAX), capturing a portion of the total trade size as follows:
- Entry Position ('Buy' Trade): 10% of the USD equivalent of the payment asset at the moment of transaction, accounted for and collected in $SEAS.
- Exit Position ('Sell' Trade): 10% of the USD equivalent of $SEAS at the moment of transaction.
Based on this txTAX component, the formula for deriving yield is directly related to real economic activity involving $SEAS, and can be defined as:
(Volume + txTAX) x Velocity
Volume, Velocity, and txTAX are defined and explained in more details below.
The Three Components of TTT
Three components/characteristics capture the essence of TTT:
- Transactional Tax (txTAX): Transaction-fee-based value accrual mechanism. Use, pay, profit.
- Volume: Total value flowing through Seasons' Yield 3.0 architecture and $SEAS tokens over time. More volume → More yield.
- Velocity: Speed or frequency at which $SEAS (or other assets in the system) switch hands. Reduces noise and enables high-quality volume.
While each fulfill its unique purpose, these components facilitate the sourcing, generation, retention, and distribution of value through Seasons.

chunks.title: TTT › Transactional Tax (txTAX)
chunks.text:
Transactional Tax (txTAX)
Seasons' fee mechanism — a.k.a. txTAX — is the kernel and starting point of Yield 3.0 model.
The txTAX component imposes a straightforward 10% fee upon entering (purchase) and exiting (sale) a $SEAS position.
Example: Say, User A buys $SEAS worth 100 USDC. With the 10% txTAX, they receive $SEAS worth ~90 USDC. Likewise, when selling 100 $SEAS, they receive USDC worth 90 $SEAS.
By taxing every transaction, Seasons ensures long-term interest alignment for holders. The txTAX deters actors with low time preference or extractive intent. Whereas by incurring a small cost in the form of a contribution to the yield-generation mechanism, aligned participants stimulate value flow and become qualified to earn from the system.
The TTT module's APY is thus comprised of the txTAX accumulated from every BUY and SELL operation involving $SEAS, accounted for and collected in real time. And to ensure equality for all participants, Seasons' imposes a unilateral txTAX regardless of transaction size or frequency.
Volume & Velocity — The 'Double Vs'
Coupled with txTAX, the 'Double Vs' — Volume and Velocity — drive Seasons' TTT module.
The oxygen for financial markets, volume is the combination of an asset's price and its trading frequency within a specific time period. Being highly reflexive in nature, volume begets more volume. When a given asset or trading pair has high volume, it generally commands more interest/demand. On the contrary, when the volume fades, demand typically fades as well.
Based on this dynamic, Seasons' mechanism is designed with volume as a core parameter facilitating yield-generation within the TTT module. It's a linear relationship, where:
Higher Volume → Higher Yield. Lower Volume → Lower Yield.
Then there's velocity, i.e., the parameter used to gauge the actual interest/demand derived from the volume component.
Velocity refers to the frequency at which a given asset — $SEAS or otherwise — switches owners (or, how many times the same address touches an asset within a given timeframe). It has an inverse relationship with ownership duration:
- Low velocity signals long-term ownership and low time preference.
- High velocity means shorter ownership duration and high time preference.
Seasons explicitly leverages the velocity component as an 'auto-immune' or defence mechanism, deterring mercenarial, malicious, or otherwise extractive entities. Coupled with the txTAX component that reduces noise to derive a more honest (and sustainable) APY, velocity dissuades market makers and similar entities from attempting market-distorting coups.
The (Volume + txTAX) x Velocity approach thus allows Seasons to serve long-term market interests. And unlike superfluous projects/products that fake their volume and other metrics, Seasons optimizes for sustainability by maximizing organic volume based on organic demand.
Asset distributions are proportionate.

chunks.title: TTT › Tax Proceed Utilization
chunks.text:
Tax Proceed Utilization
Proceeds collected through taxation are denominated in $SEAS and accumulated in the Acquirer Escrow address(es). These addresses hold the tokens until they receive an engagement signal, at which point the accumulated $SEAS is transferred to a Distributor address.
The Distributor contract/address swaps the $SEAS for assets defined in the current Inclusion Set at the time of distribution. After acquisition, the Distributor contract awaits its trigger to disseminate the acquired assets to qualified wallet addresses (Seasons Nodes).
TTT Yield Distribution
The distribution/payout modality for fee-based yield is one of Seasons' definitive features.
Traditionally, yield is paid in the same asset that the user holds, stakes, or spends to acquire the yield-bearing instrument. For example, they get more ETH by staking ETH or more USD for an U.S. Treasury bond they bought with USD.
In Seasons, however, yield is paid in a diversified basket of liquid alternative assets, each with their unique volatility profiles and archetypes. This approach unlocks a novel amplifier for return potential and expands the protocol's implied utility for users (See: How to Use Seasons).
As of March 2026, distributions happen semi-weekly (twice per week). Payout assets are sent directly to the node's wallet address, eliminating any further cost or hassle of claiming yield payouts.
The distribution frequency may change in future as the protocol matures.
TTT APY
While the TTT module doesn't have an inherent APY rate, the network-wide value generation can be summed up with the following formula:
(Volume x txFee Rate) ÷ Time
Examples of yield generated at different volumes:
1. In 365 days, at $1,000,000 in volume x 10% fee = $100,000 in yield.
2. In 365 days, at $10,000,000 in volume x 10% fee = $1,000,000 in yield.
3. In 365 days, at $100,000,000 in volume x 10% fee = $10,000,000 in yield.
4. In 365 days, at $1,000,000,000 in volume x 10% fee = $100,000,000 in yield.
Given Seasons' unique nuance where a Node is any address with a qualifying balance (i.e., 10,000+ $SEAS) — and qualifying balances are based on relative weight — individual APY depends on several constituent variables:
1. Rolling Volume
2. txfee Rate (Buy)
3. txfee Rate (Sell)
4. Node Cost (at the time of entry)
5. Relative NodeMap
6. Yield (assets)
7. Yield (strategy)
8. Time
See APY for more details on how APY is calculated within Seasons' yield mechanism.

chunks.title: TTT › Security
chunks.text:
Security
Security defines a protocol's trustworthiness. Because no matter how good a potential opportunity may seem, it holds no value unless its secure.
Seasons thus implements multi-pronged security/safety parameters: threshold triggers, shuffling escrows, and failover buffers. In addition to conducting multiple independent audits for each smart contract, Seasons has taken preemptive measures to adopt a security-first design with guardrails at every possible vector across processes, such as:
- No TVL/Management/Ownership: Seasons does not own/posses any pools or manage any assets, thereby reducing counterpart risk and removing the surface area of assets that can be swiped in the event of private key leaks or internal agent conflict.
- Yield Escrow (Acquirer/Distributor) Shuffling: Each Season has its own dedicated distributor address assigned, and sometimes even multiple distributors.
- Acquirer Slippage Stops: Slippage limits are set to ranges reflecting an asset’s category bracket (0.05%–0.25% for Blue Chips, 0.5%–1.5% for Undedogs, and 1%-5% for Rising Stars), with buffer space for moments of congestion.
F.A.Q.s
Frequently Asked Questions about the TTT module.
Q: What is the TTT?
A: TTT stands for Transactional Transfer Tax, and it is exactly what it sounds like — a fee incurred for every market/exchange interaction with the $SEAS token/yield system.
Q: What is the TTT APY?
A: Determining the APY is subject to the circumstances of each individual user, namely when they acquired their node, how much that node cost, how much volume is facilitated through $SEAS token trading, and relativity to other nodes on the network.
Q: What is the TTT Rate?
A: The current tax rate for a transaction is 10%.
Q: Can the TTT Rate change?
A: Yes. The rate can be adjusted to anything the SEASON Node Network deems to be ideal. Adaptation of the rate becomes a consideration after the instantiation of the DAO.
Q: Are all transactions subject to TTT?
A: Yes, every action involving the movement of $SEAS tokens from point A to point B triggers the TTT, including swaps (buy/sell), transfers (send/receive), and all smart contract invocations (escrow, provide LP, or locking).
Q: What happens with fees accumulated during transfers?
A: Whenever $SEAS tokens are taxed on a transfer, they do not generate fees. Having no economic significance to the network, those tokens are recycled through the YMS (Yield Management System).

chunks.title: SSYM › Basic Structure
chunks.text:
Stakeholder Stablecoin Yield Module
NOT YET ACTIVE
The SSYM shall be the second module in the Seasons Yield 3.0 system by order of implementation. After backtesting, experimental pilot programs will be conducted prior to the SSYM's instantiation. Tentatively anticipating an alpha version to be live before Q4 of 2026.
Slow, steady, and reliable, the SSYM is one of the three value drivers within the Seasons yield mechanism. Its consistent, albeit low, rate of return functions as the lower bound/base source of positive value pressure into the Seasons mechanism.
Basic Structure
A pool of proceeds is directed towards the accumulation of stablecoins (USDt, USDc, et al.). Those stablecoins are then deposited into the most secure, overcollateralized lending protocols, including, but not limited to, Jupiter and Kamino. The generated stablecoin returns are regularly injected into three tracks of the SEASONS yield mechanism, which APY returns, increase the pool's own return rate, and stimulate token velocity.
How does it work?
Trading the $SEAS token incurs a fee. Fees are generated and accounted for in $SEAS tokens at the moment of a transaction. Those fees are secured in stablecoins and deposited into the YMS. The YMS then lends out the stablecoins while they transition from yield generation to yield payout. During the period of time that they are deposited, they accrue the market-average rate of return on lending (~1-7% APY). Once the moment of the next yield distribution arrives, the deposited amount is withdrawn, minus the profits, and distributed among the nodes. Profits are then pushed through the SEASONS network.
Proceed Utilization
The SSYM utilizes its proceeds across three tracks. Given the variance of impact that each individual track provides, the exact weights of each track are subject to optimization ad hoc.
1) Yield Boosting
% is distributed with the yield distribution (apropos)
2) Reserve Strengthening
% used as a compounding vector to accelerate the absolute size of SSYM reserves
3) $SEAS BuyBack
% used to accumulate $SEAS from the open market

chunks.title: SSYM › 1) Yield Boosting
chunks.text:
1) Yield Boosting
Amplification of the total size of an individual yield distribution. This provides a smooth, small increase to each individual payout, which in turn bolsters the rate of return that a user receives.
2) Reserve Strengthening
Acceleration of the SSYM absolute reserve size. The impact of the SSYM on the SEASONS yield mechanism is linear, directly related to its size. The larger the SSYM, the more yield it generates, and the more it attracts larger market participants.
3) $SEAS Buyback
A dual service function that acquires $SEAS tokens on the open markets and removes them from circulation. The SSYM acts as a vector exerting constant positive pressure on the $SEAS token, simultaneously removing supply from orderbooks/liquidity pools while generating volume (that ultimately boosts the TTT yield module).
Controls
The SSYM belongs to the $SEAS token holders and is owned/controlled by the Seasons DAO.
In the earlier stages of the project, during the establishment of the yield mechanism and prior to the DAO's instantiation, the SSYM will require agility in its application and bootstrapping; thus, it shall not be influenced by the node networks.
Once controls are fully handed over to the DAO, token holders shall be given the ability to adjust the functionality of the SSYM as they find fit, with rights ranging from the redirection of capital flow to the ability to halt it.
Security
Given the passive liquid nature of the SSYM, it becomes an object of interest to malicious actors, internally and externally (node operators and general industry participants); thus, protective measures are instituted to preemptively mitigate subversive takeover/draining attempts.
The SSYM has no single point of operations; rather, it is a compendium of multiple independent, unrelated addresses working in orchestration. The exact address being interacted with at any moment regularly cycles amongst other addresses.
In the event a DAO decision passes to halt the SSYM, the reserves remain untouched for a preliminary period while the mechanism adjusts to its new rhythm. After the halt period elapses, another vote must be passed to deactivate and dismantle the SSYM, which will, by default, incur a prolonged emission process that ultimately deters short-term operators.

chunks.title: SSYM › F.A.Q.s
chunks.text:
F.A.Q.s
Frequently Asked Questions about the SSYM.
Q: What is the SSYM?
A: SSYM stands for Stakeholder Stablecoin Yield Module, a pool of stablecoin assets that lends through the most reliable protocols and belongs to the $SEAS token holders.
Q: What is the SSYM APY?
A: Determining the APY requires factoring in the total size and compounding rate of the SSYM. Generally, it should tread slightly above the annualized average industry lending rate.
Q: How are SSYM proceeds used?
A: Proceeds are split into three areas of Compounding, Boosting Yield, and $SEAS buybacks. The exact proportions of the split are determined based on the operating state of the project to optimize for accelerating short-term growth and the long-term impact.
Q: Can the SSYM Utilization change?
A: Yes.
Q: Can $SEAS token holder claim/withdraw/drain the SSYM?
A: TBD. Objectively, it should be entirely in the decision realm of the DAO to do as it finds fit.
Q: What assets are part of the SSYM?
A: Fiat Stablecoins. Initially, these are to be the most widespread, battle-tested, USD-denominated options, including USDc and USDt, but can be expanded to include complementary alternatives such as JupUSD, USDs, and others. Over time, more variance in the stablecoins themselves can be expected to be introduced (JPY/EURO/AED/etc.).

chunks.title: YAV › Basic Structure
chunks.text:
Yield Asset Vaults
NOT YET ACTIVE
The YAV is the third and final module in the Seasons Yield 3.0 system by order of implementation. With a wider area of application and the necessity of a dedicated orchestration layer for strategy management, the YAV component is expected to enter experimentation after the SSYM's proper integration.
One of the three core modules in the Seasons Yield 3.0 mechanism, the YAV is a smart contract that automatically deploys assets into a mixture of onchain DEFI strategies. As the module with the highest degree of technical complexity/malleability in its implementation, the YAV provides variable amplification of yield payouts.
Basic Structure
A Vault consisting of Inclusion Set assets is instantiated that belongs to Seasons (Node) Token Holders. The vault routes its holdings through a predefined DEFI strategy circuit and directs proceeds back through the Seasons network. Made accessible to the general public on alternative DEFI platforms, as well as on the Seasons terminal; the vault charges a service fee which ultimately contributes the Yield 3.0 system's returns. The embedded reflexivity features contribute to the bottom-line sustainability by ensuring persistent growth rates.
The YAV utilizes its proceeds as follows:
1) Yield assets are accumulated by Seasons Network
2) Yield assets are paired/bundled into vaults
3) Vaults are set at competitive rates to attract as much trade volume through them as possible
4) During yield distributions, yield is pulled from vaults, and proceeds accumulated through LP are injected into the Seasons Yield mechanism.
YAV Composition
The composition of the YAV is derived from the unique profiles of assets as they align with the Seasons core purpose of generating steady flows of revenue without systemic risks.
0) Prequalified by Seasons Inclusion Set Criteria
1) Reduce impacts of slippage
2) Reduce impacts of impermanent loss
3) Maximize for utilization/volume capture
4) Maximize for fee capture
In addition to possessing highly sought-after characteristics, namely liquidity, the assets must be maximally accessible and resilient against centralized counterparty failures.
Vaults are intended to be perpetual; once launched, disengaging vaults is avoided.

chunks.title: YAV › YAV Strategies
chunks.text:
YAV Strategies
Selected based on their risk profiles and return capabilities, the YAV leverages a multitude of variable DEFI strategies across the Solana blockchain ecosystem. With the surface area of opportunities constantly shifting, there are no more than 4 (four) strategies running simultaneously, each of which can be actively substituted.
Some of the Potential Strategies:
- Liquidity Provision
- Delta Neutral Fee Accumulation
- Lending
- Liquidations
Proceed Utilization
The purpose of the YAV is twofold: first, to provide a boosted return on yield by allocating a fraction of its proceeds to each network distribution, and second, to grow its own reserve of assets.
An earning period for the YAV is 72-96 hours, the time between distributions. During that block of time, the YAV generates revenue and, at the moment of the next distribution, flows across three tracks. Given the variability in impact that each individual track provides, the exact weights of each track are subject to ad hoc optimization.
1) Yield Boosting
% is distributed with the yield distribution (apropos)
2) Reserve Strengthening
% used as a compounding vector to accelerate the absolute size of YAV reserves
3) $SEAS BuyBack
% used to accumulate $SEAS from the open market
1) Yield Boosting
Steady, gradual injections of additional revenue to amplify the total size of an individual yield distribution. On top of the distribution included from the TTT and SSYM, the YAV bolsters the sum being sent; ultimately providing a smooth upwards pressure on user returns.
2) Reserve Strengthening
Ensuring consistent lower-bound growth in the TVL owned by the Vault. The impact of the YAV on the Season yield mechanism is variable, dependent foremost on its size and the return potential of applied strategies. The larger the YAV reserves, the more yield it generates, and the more it attracts larger market participants.

chunks.title: YAV › 3) $SEAS Buyback
chunks.text:
3) $SEAS Buyback
The second touchpoint for reflexive contribution to the Seasons ecosystem, the YAV spends the smallest fraction of its proceeds to exude consistent supportive open market pressure on the $SEAS token. While acquiring $SEAS from the liquidity pools and removing them from circulation, the activity triggers the TTT module, further bolstering the system's yield-generating capacity.
Controls
The YAV belongs to the $SEAS (node) token holders and is owned/controlled by the Seasons DAO. All of the vaults' self-contributed holdings constitute yield and thus belong to the network.
The DAO/Node network influences which strategies are used, how proceeds are allocated and in what proportions, and may have the option to disengage vaults and reclaim the underlying assets.
In the earlier stages of the project, during the establishment of the yield mechanism and prior to the DAO's instantiation, the YAV will require agility in its application and bootstrapping; thus, it shall not be influenced by the node networks.
F.A.Q.s
Frequently Asked Questions about the YAV.
Q: What is the YAV?
A: YAV stands for Yield Asset Vault, a smart contract that utilizes a mixture of DEFI strategies to allocate its reserves.
Q: What assets are inside the YAV?
A: Blue chip quality assets that have been/are being distributed through Seasons.
Q: Can the YAV composition change?
A: Yes, although in most situations, new Vaults are launched.
Q: How many vaults are there?
A: Theoretically, Seasons can issue vaults indefinitely; however, after the initial implementation, consecutive vault openings shall be opened only on an as-needed basis after certain quantitative criteria are met.
Q: How much APY does/can the YAV generate?
A: Variable; the APY for the YAV depends on the size
Q: How are the Vault strategies selected?
A: Based on their alignment with Seasons criteria, risk minimized, steady flow.
Q: How are the YAV earnings used?
A: Split into three parts: a portion into each yield distribution, a portion to buy more of the vault's holding assets, and a portion to buy $SEAS off the open market.
Q: How does the YAV accumulate assets?
A: Deposits from the public, deposits from yield distributions through Seasons, and vault-owned liquidity compounding.

chunks.title: Distribution › Overview
chunks.text:
Disseminating Yield
Overview
Seasons leverages a novel system for delivering proceeds throughout the SEAS Network.
Its emission configuration of where proceeds flow to, how often, what frequency value flows at, and in what form factor creates a flywheel effect on growth and sustainability; there are 2 technical factors that determine value flow, the {Node List} and the {Inclusion Set}.
Epoch Node List (Where)
The Seasons Network recognizes Solana addresses that have become Nodes as value endpoints for receiving yield. By satisfying the system's requirements, nodes are registered in the active {Epoch Node List} and automatically begin to receive yield payouts directly in their associated wallet address. No need to 'claim' and no lock-ups. Whenever a distribution event is triggered, the YMS-Acquirer/Distribution will reference the {Epoch Node List} to determine where to direct the next batch of proceeds.
Learn more about: Nodes
Inclusion Set (In what formfactor)
Seasons implements an "Inclusion Set" — a selection of liquid assets that have satisfied a predefined qualitative criteria — to determine what tokens users receive in their wallets as yield. Whenever a distribution event is engaged, the YMS will transfer the epoch's revenue to an Acquirer/Distributor, which swap everything according to the specifications in its references {Inclusion Set} prior to sending it out.
Learn more about: Inclusion Sets
Emission Size (How much/APY)
Currently, the total value of yield distributed per round operates on a rolling two-day basis [48 hours] worth of generated yield. For every 48-72-hour time period (based on the CET+1 time zone), the total yield generated is summed up and split into acquiring the inclusion set assets. The asset acquisition happens within a 24-hour time block of the actual distribution to avoid any significant shifts in price/value.
Learn more about: APY
Emission Frequency (How often)
During its initial stage, Seasons' yield distribution frequency has been set to semi-weekly (twice per week). As of March 2026, distributions happen every Sunday and Wednesday. However, this is subject to adaptation ad hoc as the protocol evolves.

chunks.title: Distribution › Epochs
chunks.text:
Epochs
An Epoch refers to a 72-96-hour period of time that applies specifically to a given distribution. The Epoch specifies from which period of time it is claiming a yield payout, the list of all qualifying $SEAS node addresses, the aggregate token balance of all qualifying yield recipients, and the amounts of each output asset that was/is distributed.
F.A.Q.s

A: No. Yield is paid out according to the specifications of the active Inclusion Set.
Q: How to claim Yield?

Q: How are the associated operating costs of distribution settled?
A: All of the system's gas consumption fees are deducted from each distribution.
Q: When is Yield Distributed?
A: The network Yield Rate is a measurement of the yield mechanism's capital efficiency and distribution capacity relative to its market valuation.
Q: What is an Epoch?
A: A period of time attributable to the specifications of a yield payout, from the amount generated during its accumulation to the balances and addresses of Nodes that specify who shall be receiving what amount.

chunks.title: Inclusion Sets › What is an Inclusion Set?

The Selection of Assets with which Yield is Distributed
A key component of the Season's yield mechanism is found in its distribution model. The distribution model involves direct-to-wallet transmissions and multi-asset output. In order to advantageously utilize this kind of dispersion mechanism, if not at the very least sustainably, careful considerations about the selection of assets that are sent out must be in place.
Automated, thorough, pre-emptive screenings to filter, categorize, and quantify opportunities by quality. Then package them into a whitelist of "Authorized Assets" for the Seasons output model to reference when engaging in a distribution, specifically the conversion to acquisition assets.
That is the process and function of the Inclusion Sets.
The determining factor in what assets are to be arriving in the user's wallet.

- No less than 2 assets included at a time
- No more than 3 assets per distribution
Inclusion Sets are further complemented by their constituent elements: Criteria, Tiers, and Suffling.
Inclusion Criteria
In order to mitigate unintended consequences of random selection and avoid malicious projects while ensuring the $SEAS yield-generating node holder base is exposed to the highest quality assets, Seasons implements a data-rich screening to QA every asset
While there are universal components/elements of the criteria for all assets, such as the history duration factored with holder counts, volumes, and trader turnover, there are also unique granular adaptations for the different tiers of inclusion Sets.
The tier grading which an asset receives and where its grading ranks in its respective tier directly determines the likelihood of its inclusion.
- Please refer to each Tier's page for deeper breakdowns.
Inclusion Tier's
Inclusion Sets are segmented into 3 tiers reflective of an asset's maturity and economic significance. Each tier has its own criteria and weight. Initially, weight distribution is determined by the Season's foundation based on the objective state of the market and return potential's balanced against risk; however, this feature functionality is among the first to be integrated into community ownership

Learn more about: Blue Chips
Under Dog's
Set Weight: 30%
Likelihood of inclusion: Under Dogs ](/seasons-docs/protocol/yield-3.0-mechanism/distribution/inclusion-lists/under-dogs-ud)

Likelihood of inclusion: Rising Stars ](/seasons-docs/protocol/yield-3.0-mechanism/distribution/inclusion-lists/rising-stars-rs)
Due to the High-Vol, High-Speed nature of the crypto industry, the likelihood of assets either potentially overlapping two tiers or shifting between them as natural market forces materialize is extremely high. Therefore, time and weight buffers are utilized to reduce variance.

chunks.title: Inclusion Sets › Set Shuffling
chunks.text:
Set Shuffling
Discovery & Substitution of active yield set.
Initially, the inclusion sets will be discovered, determined, and implemented on a Season-to-Season or Quarter-to-Quarter schedule. The duration of a Season is tentatively marked as a full Quarter of Operations (~92 days).
It is absolutely possible for Sets to be re-shuffled, meaning having the same exact asset selection be consequently specified during evaluation.
Assets to consider/process through the criteria trials are sampled at the discretion of the Season's Foundation. As the project matures, this feature function is also among the first to be conjoined with the community to participate/contribute/vote on which assets to be included.
Substitution of an asset from an active Inclusion Set can happen for a multitude of reasons, ranging from an evaporation of liquidity to moral conflict. A Supermajority of the time, should the need to remove an asset arise, the asset's slot is removed rather than replaced.
How does it work?
1. A Season is outlined {objective}
2. Potential group of Candidate/Desirable assets are aggregated into a list
3. Pre-emptive threshold filtration conducted to consolidate group into (8) that are in alignment
4. Qualifiers of Threshold move into full screening
5. Final results are reviewed and published as the "Active Inclusion Set"
6. The YMS references the "Active Inclusion Set" during every round of distribution
Angelic Inclusions
Projects interested in partnering up to gain access to Season's live on-chain holder base will be given opportunities to advance reward/incentive pools to the network of nodes. Angelic Inclusions are not factored into the yield calculations set and are proportionately added on top of the yield as a boost.
Learn more about: Angelic Inclusions
Core Qualitative Elements for Inclusions
Seasons strongly upholds the philosophies of sovereignty, freedom, and decentralization. While these terms have been monstrously abused by malicious actors and hidden behind a facade by dishonest centralized megalith corporations, Seasons has aligned itself with a pure OnChain ethos.
1) No CEX's
Assets with more than a certain percent of supply on centralized exchanges is disqualified.
2) No MM's
Assets downing in MM handling cannot be included due to extractive business models.
3) No PERPS/Leverage
Assets heavily reliant on leveraged trading lead to wipeouts that harm holders, disqualified.
4) No Cabals
Assets marked above a certain degree of cabal related activities are disqualified.
- These rigid variables notably compress the surface area of projects that can be included; therefore, a degree of context-aware, subjective manual intervention is sparingly applied to gauge things on a case-by-case basis.

chunks.title: Angelic Inclusions › Qualitative Criteria:

Asset Adoption Accelerator

Conducting an Angelic Inclusion distribution will increase the reliability/reputation of the project for any potential future inclusion list requests.

Qualitative Criteria:
While the requirements to be admitted to Angelic Distribution are relatively low, there are still measures in place to protect the community against unintentional or malicious attempts.

All four of these criteria must be met; in the event that a project's distribution is turned down, they are given the right to reapply 24 hours later. A project can apply as many times as it like, however, being rejected 3 times will disqualify it from any/all future potential inclusions.
Process
The process for Angelic Inclusion from the standpoint of a project/requester is simple and straightforward. Projects of all sizes will adhere to the same simple 5-step process outlined below:
1) Fill out the "Angelic Inclusion Request Form"

- if no deviation is detected, airdrop is conducted

chunks.title: Nodes › What are Seasons Nodes?
chunks.text:
Network Owners and Operators
What are Seasons Nodes?
Seasons Nodes are public Solana network wallet addresses that have satisfied the Yield 3.0 Mechanism's criteria and, in turn, become recognized by the Seasons network as operators. Operators are users that have proved their alignment with the Network's well-being through their fee contributions while entering a $SEAS position. By virtue of this contribution, Seasons Network endows them with operational and ownership rights.
Functions & Capabilities
Nodes are seen and treated as Owners by the Seasons network; therefore, they are granted a substantial amount of influence over it, namely in the form of irrefutable claims on the capital flows. Becoming endpoints where the Yield 3.0 mechanism deposits its Liquidity in order to direct how/where the liquidity goes; Nodes can harvest the yield, compound their rates, or redirect it altogether.
Ownership comes with responsibility. In Seasons, that responsibility is materialized in the form of stewardship. Shepherding the protocol to its healthiest possible version/state. Nodes constantly make decisions that directly influence the protocol's short- and long-term capacities and capabilities.
Asset Routing
As yield is dispersed throughout the network, nodes have the final decision on whether or not and how the Seasons yield mechanism handles liquidity. They can redirect flows immediately to help smooth out the mechanism, or harvest the proceeds for delayed deployment under the assumption the proceeds will grow independently. They can entirely deflect the flows and extract the value for external (independent/unrelated) purposes.
Mechanism Configuration
Influence elements of the Yield 3.0 system's operations. The Yield 3.0 Mechanism possesses a multitude of gauges and formulas that can be adjusted in order to augment the protocol's operations. From the service fee charged by the TTT, to the SSYM's proceeds weight utilization, to the YAV's compositions, and everything in between (even the distribution rates); roughly 40 elements are available for collaborative construction.

chunks.title: Nodes › DAO membership

chunks.title: Nodes › Node Ledger
chunks.text:
Node Ledger
The Seasons Node Ledger is a registry in the form of a smart contract database containing the state of network operators. Derived as a subset from the $SEAS token smart contract, the registry monitors the holder data and records all state changes in real time.
The Ledger provides the following [ 8 ] data points:
- Address
- Type
- Balance
- Weight
- Age
- (DOA) date of activation
- Latest Payout
- Next Payout
Access
The Node Ledger can be queried at any time to provide a snapshot of the Nodes. In order to query the Node Ledger, users can:
- use the "Node Registrar" in the terminal
- interact with GAIA
Sequencing
There are no preferences, multipliers, or tiers. Regardless of size, behavior, or age, all nodes on Seasons are treated equally when it comes to consideration for timing or order of yield distribution. Yield is dispersed sequentially to how/when it is accrued.
F.A.Q.s
Frequently Asked Questions about Nodes.
Q: What is a Season's Node?
A: Season's nodes are Solana network/chain wallet addresses that generate yield.
Q: What is the Seasons Node Ledger?
A: The Node Ledger is the smart contract database that keeps a live record of nodes.
Q: How many Types of Nodes are there?
A: There are two (2) types of nodes; Director nodes and Builder nodes
Q: What is the potential APY of a node?
A: APY's of nodes are subject to the unique circumstances of each individual node instance and the momentum flowing through the Seasons network.
Q: Can 1 address own multiple Nodes?
A: No. Strict adherence to a 1 address = 1 node policy.
Q: Can I sell my tokens and still generate yield?
A: Yes, so long as the balance of a wallet is above the threshold 1k/10k level of $SEAS token, it will continue generating yield.
Q: What assets do Nodes generate?
A: That depends on the type of node and the specifications of the "Inclusion Set" at the time of acquisition/distribution.

chunks.title: Director Nodes › Director Yield
chunks.text:
Director Yield
Director nodes accrue yield in the form of a twice-weekly, direct-to-wallet liquidity deposit in a predefined basket of assets outlined in the Inclusion Set. A Director's core intentions align with routing where and how the mechanism's liquidity flows.
Director Yield Implementation v2:
Frequency: 2x per week
Events: Sunday & Wednesday
Asset: Perfect Order (IS Asset Basket)
Rate: Full (network velocity×weight)
Type: Direct Distributions
A defining feature of a Director Node is the automated distributions of yield directly to their wallet addresses. By removing the need to remember to claim, pay fees, or deal with any form of vesting, directors are encouraged to engage with as much of the mechanism as possible without incurring opex.
APY Rate
The multi-dimensional, dynamic nature of the Yield 3.0 engine produces circumstantial variance around the APY of any individual node, causing rates to fluctuate. Therefore, distilling APY requires a historical trail and an estimated understanding of the network's forward-looking capital bandwidth and velocity.
Director node APYs are a function derived from the global Network APY;
{( $ TTT dis + $ SSYM dis + $ YAV dis ) / (NodeSPEC/NodeSTATE)}
- A generalized model and deeper explanation can be found here in the APY section .
An over-simplified breakdown of the factors impacting a Director's APY rate are as follows:
Time/Cost of Node at Joining
Network Performance since Joining
Global State of All Nodes in the Network
Relative Weight of Node vs Network
Node Weights
As one of the most impactful factors in determining the balancing of yield flows, a Director Node's weight represents its relative $SEAS token position size as a percentage ratio to the total amount of $SEAS tokens balances on all active Director Nodes at a given distribution epoch.
Weight is determined by:
1. Adding all $SEAS token balances of active Builder nodes
2. Dividing an individual Builder's balance by the aggregate sum
Director Node Weights are relative only to Director Nodes.
$SEAS balance Director wallet/address ÷ all $SEAS on All Directorsin yield period
The weight of a Node represents its relative claim size as a percentage allocation of the yield distribution, determining the portion attributable to it at that distribution event; the larger the weight, the larger the portion of a distribution.
Example:
5 nodes have a shared balance of 100,000 tokens.
Wallet-A has 10,000 $SEAS (10%)
Wallet-B has 12,500 $SEAS (12.5%)
Wallet-C has 12,500 $SEAS (12.5%)
Wallet-D has 25,000 $SEAS (25%)
Wallet-E has 40,000 $SEAS (40%)
Since the total sum of $SEAS token balances on nodes is 100,000, each individual node's share of the revenue stream is (their balance $1,000)
Wallet-A weighs 0.1 (10%)
Wallet-B weighs 0.125 (12.5%)
Wallet-C weighs 0.125 (12.5%)
Wallet-D weighs 0.25 (25%)
Wallet-E weighs 0.4 (40%)
A $1,000 Yield Distribution takes place (epoch # 341)
Wallet-A receives $100 (10%)
Wallet-B receives $125 (12.5%)
Wallet-C receives $125 (12.5%)
Wallet-D receives $250 (25%)
Wallet-E receives $400 (40%)
While any individual node's balance does not materially impact the liquidity being routed at any given moment, the amalgamation of all balances on all Director Nodes will ultimately determine how much liquidity is dispersed to any single node and in what proportion.
Example: Wallet-A has 12,000 $SEAS during an epoch where the total $SEAS balance in the yield system is 24,000. Thus, Wallet-A's node weight is: 12,000 ÷ 24,000 = 0.5.
Director nodes' yield is sourced from the proceeds generated by the Yield 3.0 mechanism between distribution events. Each of the modules accumulates revenue from its own unique purpose, then the proceeds are aggregated, converted, and disseminated( see: APY)

Learn more about: Seasons DAO
Deactivation
To halt the stream of yield, a node must be decomposed by reducing the balance of the wallet to below 10,000 tokens. Falling below 10,000 tokens (either by sending or selling) will automatically remove the wallet address from the distribution ledger, tag it as archived, and recalibrate the next distribution epoch accordingly.
Node deactivation implies the conduction of a transaction, which, by virtue of design logic baked into the $SEAS token contract, shall engage the TTT and incur a fee. In the event that a wallet, for whatever reason, dips below the threshold but manages to return above within a yield window, they retain their position.

Frequently Asked Questions about Director Nodes.

A: Director nodes are the Owners and Operators of the Seasons Network/Yield 3.0 Mechanism; any non-blacklisted Solana wallet addresses that generate yield by holding at least 10,000 tokens.

A: Subjective and circumstantial; the APY of a node is determined by a multitude of factors acting in orchestration with each other. Seasons aims to achieve consistency within its target range of 6.58%-21.07%; however, variance outside of it is to be expected.
Q: Should I split a Node if it has over 10,000 tokens?
A: It is a matter of preference and wallet management. All nodes are treated equally. Whether it is one address with 20,000 tokens or 2 addresses with 10,000 tokens each, they will generate equally proportional yield.

A: Yes, so long as the balance of your wallet is above 10,000 $SEAS, you will continue generating yield.

A: Yes, in the event a director chooses to regress into a Builder, the transition will incur an attribution delay until the following distribution event.

A: Yes, Builders can/do graduate into Directors as outlined in the "Builder Nodes" section of this document.
Q: Does an address have to be a Builder before becoming a Director?
A: No. If an operator chooses to become a director right away, they can do so without having to be a Builder.

chunks.text:
Builder Yield
Builder nodes accrue a different type of yield than Directors do entirely. A Builder's core intention is to increase its holdings of $SEAS tokens in order to grow large enough to ultimately become a Director; thus, Builders' entire yield is earned exclusively in $SEAS tokens.
Builder Yield Implementation v1:
Frequency: 1x per week
Events: Sunday
Asset: $SEAS
Rate: APY×0.8
Type: Claim
Builders generate their yield in real-time, in tandem with the Season's network APY. Generated yield is accumulated and released once per week; every Sunday after Director Yield Distributions conclude.
As part of their contributions on the path to graduation, Builders help propagate the Seasons' on-chain footprint by regularly triggering a $SEAS-branded smart contract to collect their yield.
Yield Source
Builder Nodes' yield is tertiary in order; it is dependent on the yield of the Directors, which ultimately is itself a by-product of the Yield 3.0 mechanism's velocity.
The yield for builders is sourced from $SEAS network subsidies; a limited, dedicated $SEAS token supply allocation directed toward (operator) community and growth. These subsidies are pooled and deployed in phases, intended to assist in bootstrapping a multi-type-node environment and bringing more $SEAS token supply into activation.
It is assumed that a Builder Node's balance and its chronological placement in the token holder list are always growing in alignment with its overarching purpose of becoming a Director. The first iterations exploring a Builder Node implementation are heavily rooted in game theory assumptions in operator behavior (doing everything possible to accelerate growth and minimize setbacks (i.e., avoid leaving their position).
Ultimately, assuming that tangible value from the Builder component is prescient, Builder Yield sustainability hinges on embedding end-to-end flows from operations. Some of the tentative Sustainability Options and circular funding models include pool-based options such as:
- non-trade-transfer fee share
- TTT redirection
- SSYM/YAV re-allocation

This ratio establishes the relative proportions of a distribution. The larger the weight, the larger the portion of a distribution.

The yield-payout allocation for a given node is determined by its relative weight within the distribution epoch. Nodes thus receive yield in proportion to their $SEAS holding compared to the total amount of "qualified" tokens within that payout period, which is calculated as:
$SEAS balance of the wallet/address ÷ all $SEAS tokens in the yield period (epoch)
Graduation
The graduation process and all of its implications are actively under consideration. From additional on-chain gas costs to deterring inequality, it is to be expected that, while the graduation process is under revision, it is likely to change or even be subject to total removal.
The process of transitioning from a Builder to a Director node is known as graduation. Graduation occurs the moment a Builder Node exceeds the scope of criteria {A} by having its balance tick past 10,000 $SEAS tokens.
Graduating Nodes are faced with the dilemma of contribution size. Given that being a Director has its own requirement of a 1,000 $SEAS tokens minimum while entering a position, but a Builder most likely will not (assuming no defective behavior). Therefore, this requirement is levied and arbitrated out with the alternative time contribution or either 183 consecutive days or an aggregate of 365 days of being a builder.

chunks.title: APY › Determining Node APY
chunks.text:
Determining Seasons Annual Percentage Yield Potential
While to some degree reliant on the overall sentiment of the economy (as is any instrument, business, or industry), SEASONS APY is derived through an amalgamation of three (3) value-generating channels that are independent from one another. The driving forces of each channel imply distinct rate-of-return and risk profiles, in turn increasing variance and positioning the SEASONS Yield system apart from other solutions on the market.
- TTT - generation of revenue based on trading activity
- SSYM - generation of revenue based on industry lending rates
- YAV - generation of revenue based on fees accrued from the provision of liquidity.
Unlike the yield generated from traditional vehicles, SEASONS yield is derived from socio-economic vectors unrelated to government/legacy instruments; this breakage of dependency links introduces a new capacity for yield, one that is highly subjective, variable, and volatile.
Given the multi-depth variances of not just the dynamic source of yield but the dynamism of the type of yield, Season's utilizes a novel Elastic framework to establish APY.
Determining Node APY
APY in Season's is established by aggregating the output revenue being generated by each of its yield channels across two dimensions: a Network's APY/YR and the Individual $SEAS node APY.
The best expression can be found in an empirical simulation as follows:
Annualized distributions: $3,500,000 + $650,000 of upwards pressure on value
- TTT - $3,000,000 distributions
- SSYM - $200,000 distributions + $300,000 anscillary impact
- YAV - $300,000 distributions + $350,000 anscillary impact
If TTT facilitates $30,000,000 in volume and generates $3,000,000 in fees, of which the entire amount is distributed, then this channel produces $3,000,000 in annualized distributions.
If SSYM holdings $10,000,000 in USDc and generates $500,000, of which $200,000 is distributed as yield, $150,000 of which buys back $SEAS tokens (contributing $15,000 in TTT revenue), and $150,000 of which goes to increasing the size of the SSYM, then this channel produces $200,000 in annualized distributions.
If the YAV has $10,000,000 in asset TVL and facilitates enough trade activity to generate $650,000 in annualized fees, of which $300,000 is distributed as yield, $175,000 of which buys back $SEAS tokens (contributing $17,500 in TTT revenue), and $175,000 of which goes to increasing the YAV TVL, then this channel produces $300,000 in annualized distributions.
Under the assumption that there are 1,000 nodes, all of which entered at the same base cost of $5,000 and possess equal balances over time, then each node will receive an equal portion of the $3,500,000 or $3,500; and an APY of approximately ~70%. (without factoring in the growth reserve and potential of token volatility).
The formula can be applied to fit any number of assumptions:
( $ TTT dis + $ SSYM dis + $ YAV dis ) / (Node/NodeSTATE) = APY of node

chunks.title: APY › Network APY (YR)
chunks.text:
Network APY (YR)
The network itself does not have an APY rate; it has a base YR (yield generation rate). The Yield generation rate is a by-product of the total annual yield SEASONS distributes as measured against its market presence. The YR serves as a gauge for evaluating the well-being of the $SEAS token.
Building on the above assumptions of $3,500,000 in distributions and a base node entry spot price of $0.50 ($500m FDV), the YR can be established by simply dividing the FDV by the distributions and then dividing it again by 10 to arrive at a YR of 14.28571428571429
YR modeling:
At $10,000,000 distributions x $100,000,000 FDV = YR 1
At $7,000,000 distributions x $350,000,000 FDV = YR 5
At $5,000,000 distributions x $500,000,000 FDV = YR 10
At $4,000,000 distributions x $800,000,000 FDV = YR 20
Generally, the YR should be in the 5-25 range. Everything outside of that range would indicate a logical value discrepancy.
The lower the YR, the higher the value proposition to own a node and, in turn, the incentive to drive demand market activity of $SEAS. Inversely, the higher the YR, the more overheated the competition between nodes over the same pool of capital, incentivizing supply-driven market activity.
Elastic APY
The yield generated/distributed by Seasons is dynamic and highly susceptible to changes on a per-distribution basis.
There are five (5) factors for the estimation of yield:
- Total # of nodes + total # of $SEAS tokens on all nodes
- Relative epoch weight of reciever:total amount of epoch $SEAS tokens
- Volume of $SEAS transactions from applicable time block of yield payout
- Total # of stablecoins in SSYM + current lending rate
- Total # of Vault assets in YAV + current LP rate
Each one of these 5 factors is in constant flux, creating variance in a progressive climb amid a steady recursive compounding.

Accessing Yield
The consumer path is a short-lived, singular inclusion into the Node set, whereby an address must acquire $SEAS off the open market and burn it. As soon as an address burns the $SEAS, it is added into the upcoming distribution mold and receives a portion of the distribution. This function treats a single burn transaction as minimal node weight or exactly 10,000 tokens. This function can be called once per address per round of yield distribution. Establishing the circulating supply of $SEAS token is augmented by the Seasons' token native unit transfer tax. A multitude of operational nuances during the execution of any transaction demand an interim class/type of supply, "immobile". Immobile refers to the state of a lock-supply currently in the YMS. Immediately at the moment of token genesis, the initial allocation process incurs a fee on every transfer, which accrues back to the YMS but ultimately belongs to the allocation. All system balance calibrations, token locks, liquidity adjustments, reward distributions, Acquirer coordinations, et al, cause occasional balance bloats by temporarily increasing the YMS $SEAS holdings.
Allocation
The total and maximum $SEAS token supply of 1,000,000,000 (1 billion) was emitted at genesis. The tokens' mint function has been revoked to forgo any potential inflationary forces.
The initial distribution required the YMS's looped logic to achieve equilibrium through a recursive re-distribution across all seven (7) segments. Each allocation segment is granulated across a multitude of wallets based on use case, and the holding wallets are assigned their own lock period.
Allocaton | % Supply | # Tokens
Liquidity | 10% | 100,000,000
Privates | 20% | 200,000,000
Foundation | 25% | 250,000,000
Public | 25% | 250,000,000
Team | 5% | 50,000,000
Incentives | 5% | 50,000,000

Totals | 100% | 1,000,000,000
When $SEAS tokens are allocated, their movement triggers the transfer fee function, which redirects 10% to the YMS. The YMS is tasked with filtration and identification of such flows to compartmentalize the transaction resulting impact; either receiving an "operational" tag for temporary partial custody of the supply supplementing (which does not spread the flow into yield) or as a market transaction (which does get pushed to yield).
This same logic applies to locking tokens.
Once tokens arrive at their holding addresses, nominated accounts then lock and remove some amount from circulation. When implementing a lock, a transfer is required, in turn activating the fee. After locks mature, they return their $SEAS tokens to the token account of the locking address; once again, invoking a 10% fee. These fees are captured by the YMS and are classified as operational; at the moment of a supply unlock, the YMS will inject the fees back into its originating source. A: Yield quantity is derived from 4 main variables;

- Sell Volume
- Number of "nodes" (active yielder's)
- Rolling auto-yield

A: The transactional Tax is a fee attached to every open on-chain market operations that involves the $SEAS token. The fee is captured and redirected throughout the Season's nodes.

A: Tier weights are ascribed in proportion to their potential risk and return; in the first iteration they shall not be changed. However, they are absolutely susceptible to change at a later date, potential by community request via DAO.

(more information shall be provided in the Yield System --> Stable Baseline section)

Nevertheless, at a certain point of the product's maturity it is anticipated that the community might be included to publicize it in the name of true openness; if/when they so decide to, the formulas will be provided via ZK for them to act upon it.

A: Absolutely. Q: Will Yield always be paid in the same tokens?
A: No. Yield is paid out according to the specifications of the active Inclusion Set.
Q: What is an Epoch?
A: A period of time attributable to the specifications of a yield payout, from the amount generated during its accumulation to the balances and addresses of Nodes that specify who shall be receiving what amount.
TTT
Frequently Asked Questions about the TTT.
Q: What is the TTT?
A: TTT stands for Transactional Transfer Tax, and it is exactly what it sounds like — a fee incurred for every market/exchange interaction with the $SEAS token/yield system.
Q: What is the TTT APY?
A: Determining the APY is subject to the circumstances of each individual user, namely when they acquired their node, how much that node cost, how much volume is facilitated through $SEAS token trading, and relativity to other nodes on the network.
Q: What is the TTT Rate?
A: The current tax rate for a transaction is 10%.
Q: Can the TTT Rate change?
A: Yes. The rate can be adjusted to anything the SEASON Node Network deems to be ideal. Adaptation of the rate becomes a consideration after the instantiation of the DAO.
Q: Are all transactions subject to TTT?
A: Yes, every action involving the movement of $SEAS tokens from point A to point B triggers the TTT, including swaps (buy/sell), transfers (send/receive), and all smart contract invocations (escrow, provide LP, or locking).
Q: What happens with fees accumulated during transfers?
A: Whenever $SEAS tokens are taxed on a transfer, they do not generate fees. Having no economic significance to the network, those tokens are recycled through the YMS (Yield Management System).

chunks.title: F.A.Q.s › SSYM

SSYM
Frequently Asked Questions about the SSYM.
Q: What is the SSYM?
A: SSYM stands for Stakeholder Stablecoin Yield Module, a pool of stablecoin assets that lends through the most reliable protocols and belongs to the $SEAS token holders.
Q: What is the SSYM APY?
A: Determining the APY requires factoring in the total size and compounding rate of the SSYM. Generally, it should tread slightly above the annualized average industry lending rate.
Q: How are SSYM proceeds used?
A: Proceeds are split into three areas of Compounding, Boosting Yield, and $SEAS buybacks. The exact proportions of the split are determined based on the operating state of the project to optimize for accelerating short-term growth and the long-term impact.
Q: Can the SSYM Utilization change?
A: Yes.
Q: Can $SEAS token holder claim/withdraw/drain the SSYM?
A: TBD. Objectively, it should be entirely in the decision realm of the DAO to do as it finds fit.
Q: What assets are part of the SSYM?
A: Fiat Stablecoins. Initially, these are to be the most widespread, battle-tested, USD-denominated options, including USDc and USDt, but can be expanded to include complementary alternatives such as JupUSD, USDs, and others. Over time, more variance in the stablecoins themselves can be expected to be introduced (JPY/EURO/AED/etc.).
YAV
Frequently Asked Questions about the YAV.
Q: What is the YAV?
A: YAV stands for Yield Asset Vault, a smart contract that utilizes a mixture of DEFI strategies to allocate its reserves.
Q: What assets are inside the YAV?
A: Blue chip quality assets that have been/are being distributed through Seasons.
Q: Can the YAV composition change?
A: Yes, although in most situations, new Vaults are launched.
Q: How many vaults are there?
A: Theoretically, Seasons can issue vaults indefinitely; however, after the initial implementation, consecutive vault openings shall be opened only on an as-needed basis after certain quantitative criteria are met.
Q: How much APY does/can the YAV generate?
A: Variable; the APY for the YAV depends on the size
Q: How are the Vault strategies selected?
A: Based on their alignment with Seasons criteria, risk minimized, steady flow.
Q: How are the YAV earnings used?
A: Split into three parts: a portion into each yield distribution, a portion to buy more of the vault's holding assets, and a portion to buy $SEAS off the open market.
Q: How does the YAV accumulate assets?
A: Deposits from the public, deposits from yield distributions through Seasons, and vault-owned liquidity compounding.
