Many of these objectives are overlapping; to some degree, depending on and determining one another. While others are means by which we expand the surface area of the $SEAS token, capturing as much trading activity as possible, and maximizing the yield for node holders.
We don’t expect to achieve every target immediately, but we know we’ll achieve them definitively…
One by one,
and then, all at once.
Let’s roll.

chunks.title: 2026 › 1) Reach 1,000,000 followers across social platforms
chunks.text:
1) Reach 1,000,000 followers across social platforms
Honing our focus on 7 channels across 6 platforms (Twitter/X (http://x.com/SEAS_onchain), Telegram (https://t.me/SeasonsCommunity), LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/company/seasons-seas), YouTube (https://www.youtube.com/@SEAS_onchain), Substack (https://seasonchain.substack.com/publish/home), and Medium (https://medium.com/seasons-blog)), we intend to provide content in all consumable formats and connect with as wide an audience as possible. While raw follower numbers do not necessitate conversion, they do amplify the message and provide a rigorous feedback loop.
2) Build up $4,000,000 in liquidity
As the lifeblood of trading activity, higher levels of liquidity for the $SEAS token will establish a higher bandwidth to sustain larger trades and, in turn, attract entities capable of executing such trades. Liquidity buildup will potentially be conducted in multiple assets but accounted for in stablecoins.
3) Surpass $100,000,000 in trading volume
Measured equally and bi-directionally with both BUY and SELL side transactions, volume is the kernel of Seasons’ mechanism, with volume as the de facto parameter gauging market interest and fueling yield. Given the absence of CEXs and presence of the velocity buffer against wash-trading MM activity, achieving this target will put a spotlight on the true organic capacity of the internet/crypto economy.
4) Distribute $10,000,000 in yield
Going hand-in-hand with the preceding objective of volume, the value of distributed yield is directly correlated with the amount of $SEAS tokens being traded. With more trades, more value flows back to Seasons nodes as yield, which increases the value (and desirability) of owning each node.
5) Secure at least 24 partnerships
Another target that’s numerically defined, but qualitatively focused. We’re committed to building strong and lasting strategic relationships with project operators. Going beyond surface-level ‘handshakes’, we shall strive to improve the lives of every community interacting with Seasons.
6) Scale beyond 1,000 nodes
Nodes are where yield flows. Too few nodes may lead to a hyper-condensed ROI, with maximally extractive behavior. Too many nodes can dampen the ROI. We believe having 1,000 nodes that earn superior yields is the sweet spot where Seasons can make a measurable, positive impact on the lives of its users globally.

chunks.title: 2026 › 7) Surpass 20,000 holders
chunks.text:
7) Surpass 20,000 holders
More $SEAS holders make Seasons more reliable from a social standpoint. By increasing the number of Seasons nodes, we aim to attract more general and speculative holders who can fuel trading volume, and thereby yield. While this is numerically a low-fidelity metric, it’s impossible to ignore when coupled with the real, global community we’re building for Seasons.
8) Surpass 250,000 transactions
Transaction counts, especially on a low-cost chain like Solana, does not carry much weight on its own. But when each transaction is amortized against the total volume, interesting behavioral patterns begin to arise. This enables a finer understanding of the user profile to which an asset such as $SEAS appeals the most
And when transactions express repetitive addresses, the $SEAS token takes on a different role—beyond speculation and beyond bearing yield, it becomes a colloquial “piggy bank”. We believe we will achieve this target with relative ease.
9) Expand the market footprint of $SEAS and Seasons
A project’s market footprint includes variables like tradable asset pairs, directory listings, and transactional visibility. As Seasons matures and our community grows, we aim to further expand the presence of $SEAS tokens. To this end, we will drive economic visibility across every possible sector.
10) Release our Dashboard v0.1
One of the most exciting elements awaiting Seasons in 2026, we will be releasing a front-end to empower users with greater “digital tangibility”. While we’re building an end-to-end tokenized product that abstracts away all complexities related to handling the asset/product, it has become obvious to us that our users require stronger touchpoints for engagement.
The degree of the dashboard’s development (in terms of functionality) is to be determined. But the most important analytic function shall definitely be produced this year.
11) Establish custom analytics for Seasons
Providing granular information about yield flows and other key protocol metrics is the cornerstone of Seasons’ effectiveness as a product. We aim to achieve this via the Dashboard mentioned above, initiating a recursive flywheel that attracts users and partner projects.
But Solana is notorious for its data-divergence. Identifying and sourcing accurate, reliable data is challenging on the Solana Network (for now). We shall overcome this by implementing our custom analytics framework to consolidate the necessary information and provide users with a coherent, complete picture through the Dashboard.

chunks.title: 2026 › 12) Publish the “SOY 2026 — State of Yield 2026” report
chunks.text:
12) Publish the “SOY 2026 — State of Yield 2026” report
To help foster a more compelling image and solidify Seasons’ positioning as a leader in global finance, we will publish our first (of many) research report in 2026, outlining the current state of yield across traditional and crypto-native finance.
This report will educate readers on how value flows through financial systems as yield and the key obstacles in this regard, while quantifying the opportunity at hand and shedding light on Seasons’ vision for a change.
13) Launch Season 2 — A new season
No, we don’t mean a new token (or do we…)—we mean introducing a new segment/category of yield.
Since genesis, Seasons’ default setting for yield payouts is meme-based. Simple, clean, compliant, and but with immensely high beta.
Based on the data generated from this default setting throughout this year, we anticipate an opportunity to introduce a new category of assets for yield payouts, with radically different value/risk profiles. This will attract new users, new partners, and increase Seasons’ overall value proposition for the industry at large.
14) Enhance the logical circuits of Seasons’ smart contracts
We’re constantly fine-tuning and improving the Seasons protocol and its tokenized yield mechanism.
From automating yield acquisition and distribution pipelines, systematizing data-based processes, and ironing out timing discrepancies to improving the weighing functions and enhancing rewards, alignment for users and even introducing new smart contracts to reduce costs or better share control rights with nodes—there’s an incredible amount of work to be done. 2026 is the builders’ year!
15) Conduct token and protocol audits
Token audits shall be conducted simply as a formality. However, auditing the system components and their inter-operational relationships is a fundamentally important element for the security of the project/product.
16) Expand $SEAS integrations
This one covers technical partnerships that touch both integrations with the $SEAS token, as well as the yield system itself. Be it a high-frequency opportunity, such as a payment provider, or a high-margin opportunity, such as a betting house, we will explore and tap into every viable option to drive utilization for Seasons’ four-pronged product(s).

chunks.title: 2026 › 17) Deploy Seasons’ multi-chain iteration
chunks.text:
17) Deploy Seasons’ multi-chain iteration
Solana is home. It’s where Seasons was born and where it shall always remain. Nevertheless, the internet economy is growing its population across different ecosystems and ignoring them would be detracting from the opportunities to provide a wider selection of assets and invite wider groups of node owners.
And technically, Seasons is a chain-agnostic protocol that can thrive equally well on any robust blockchain. So to unleash its full potential, we will pursue a multi-chain deployment strategy at some point in 2026.
18) Onboard Tier-1 operators and strategic partners
Strategic partnerships are powerful tools that can accelerate outputs by order of magnitude, improve products, and reduce errors tremendously. We intend to open conversations with as many sophisticated long-term operators that are interested in building user-centric and impact-driven solutions with Seasons.
19) Activate the B2B component
Actively propagating the opportunity for projects to get their assets placed into the Seasons Inclusions lists will bolster the project's revenue, expand the suite of options for yield-earning nodes, and transform the post-launch strategies for operators. We will actively engage in the expansion of our inclusion list throughout 2026.
20) Grow the Seasons’ team
As Seasons accelerates, the implied growth will require additional skilled/talented individuals to join the team. Currently earmarking roles in the realms of business and tech development for support with campaign and partnership management, smart contract optimization, systems automation, security, and data engineering, the Seasons family is staged to grow this year, along with the protocol and our global community.
21) Amplify the Seasons namespace
A strong and vibrant online presence is the cornerstone of success for any project, company, or business in today’s time. Discoverability builds trust; the easier it is to find you and know about you, the easier it is to trust you.
Besides focusing on SEO and AEO, this year we will triple our efforts to capture as much digital real estate as possible, across official and team channels. Some of the initiatives will include increasing the amount and frequency of our publications, as well as the depth/scope of information we deliver. Others will include collaborative efforts with external partners, ambassadors, and so on.

chunks.title: 2026 › 22) Grow the Seasons Ambassador Program
chunks.text:
22) Grow the Seasons Ambassador Program
Joining forces with capable, reliable, and driven independent influencers that are aligned with the Seasons’ mission, vision, and philosophy further strengthens the organic reach and impact of the our product.
We have already soft-launched an alpha ambassador program after announcing it on a Twitter/X spaces AMA with the awesome team at Scribble. We anticipate that this program will grow substantially as the operational infrastructure to support/manage it is refined.
Rather than putting an arbitrary number of ambassadors and then pursuing a numeric target just for the sake of hitting it, we’re focusing on the qualitative aspects of the program’s growth, such as strengthening a dedicated core group of ambassadors with better educational material or marketing support.
23) Implement our AI-guide
In part an effort to widen the breadth of content form factors while simultaneously leaning into the massive demand for agentic AI, we are compiling a “blog pseudo-podcast” to serve as an autonomous guide for users.
24) Increase our presence at events
Joining well-recognized events such as Token2049 Dubai, Token2049 Singapore, Future Blockchain Summit, WebX, Breakpoint, among others, leads to heightened awareness amongst operators within the Industry.
In the context of Seasons, however, ‘industry’ is not limited to generalized crypto, blockchain, and web3. Alternative sectors, including traditional finance, are also up for consideration.
The exact manner and capacity of our event participation is to be determined based on availability and ultimately impact. That said, as of January 5, 2026, we’re more interested in presenting the project on-stage, through founder panels and keynotes, than operating booths.
25) Accelerate the Seasons’ Brand-IP
Seasons is the namesake of nature itself. Many of the world's largest brands carry the ethereal essence of super-fluid-cycle changes.
Winter, Summer, Spring, Fall. 2026 will be a year where efforts are exerted in defending the project across all vectors, product, system, brand identity and beyond.
26) Instantiate the SRL (Seasons Research Lab)
Information is the driver of discovery. The SRL (Seasons Research Lab) will be a branch of Seasons, dedicated to conducting deep analysis on the DeFi industry and publishing its research for the public. The efforts of the SRL contribute to the evolution of the product while providing an independent arm for data-driven content.
2025 was an important year. It was the year Seasons was born.
The future is uncertain. We don’t know what happens when…
But we do know that no matter what the headlines may say, the future is brighter than it has ever been in the history of mankind.
The only way to predict the future,
is to build it yourself.
Onwards

Ideas on using Seasons Yield
The below strategies are merely suggestions and should be treated at such; this is not an endorsement or encouragement for the public to replicate; these are simply strategies that have proven effective during simulation and retroactive testing.
Due to the unique design of the Season's system, it can be an excellent alternative/addition to a balanced, diversified portfolio strategy. While there are numerous potential implementations that can augment returns beyond traditional tools, the options provided below are varied based on risk, return potential, and degree of user involvement.
These strategies are based on the fundamental potential operation and do not factor in the price of the $SEAS token! Users should make their own assumptions on how any given strategy will augment their yield.
Each strategy is accompanied by a description and 4 explainer vectors that evaluate concept, impact, time preference, and management. Each strategy can be implemented in isolation or combined with others to further increase the variability of its impact.
Concept: Simple explanation of the Strategy
Impact: How much the strategy can affect the APY
Time Preference: How long a user expects to/can be involved
Management: The amount of manual/active involvement necessary from the user's side to implement.
1 Strategy 1 : "Yield-Bonding"
Concept: Hold on to assets generated via Yield
Impact: Heavy
Time preference: Long/Undetermined
Management: Near none, passive monitoring
Description: Most effective for those looking to leverage a speculative informational edge, build a portfolio, or those with prolonged time horizons. Colloquially referred to as "Yield-bonding"; the first strategy is a simple set-it-and-forget-it method with exponential impact on the APY of a $SEAS Seasons holder's portfolio. Yield Bonding adds the additional variables of dynamisms inherent to the assets generated through yield; binding the user's APY to the value of the yield; if the yield grows in value, so does the user's APY, likewise, in the event the assets devalue, the user's APY moves in tandem.

chunks.title: Strategic Repository › 2Strategy 2: "Yield-Locking"
chunks.text:
2Strategy 2: "Yield-Locking"
Concept: Sell yielded assets off into Stablecoins
Impact: Low
Time preference: Short/Immediate
Management: Low planned engagement
Description: The most conservative approach for $SEAS yield. By converting all generated yield at a set cadence (once per day) or immediately upon receiving it, the APY becomes somewhat more linear, enabling a higher degree of predictability in a portfolio. By muting volatility, "Yield-Locking" becomes an excellent option for users intent on building cash reserves or as a source of spending resources.
3 Strategy 3 : "Yield-Compounding"
Concept: Swap Yield into $SEAS
Impact: Exponential
Time preference: Long/Undetermined
Management: Active & Passive (auto-function activation at user discretion, planned development)
Description: Accelerant/amplifier of $SEAS Yield system, best for users looking to augment the rate of yield accrual. As the name might suggest, Yield Compounding is a strategy focused on growing the momentum at which yield is generated. By increasing the $SEAS position itself, the relative weight of a user/address grows and, in turn, captures a larger portion of yield.
4 Strategy 4 : "Yield-Speculation"
Concept: Swap Yield into other Assets
Impact: Exponential
Time preference: Short/Immediate
Management: Hyper-active
Description: Effectively a way to de-risk by putting earned yield directly to work. As a managed source to fund trading activities, whereby yield turns into a tool to amplify speculative gains. This is not a direct way to augment APY, it is a way to augment a total financial strategy.

Season's is an adaptation of these mechanisms that induces the sharing of proceeds throughout the system's network unilaterally and perpetually. Given that yield is generated for the user through the efforts of other users, the incentives of participants are aligned to promote activity (velocity).

Requirements
By virtue of the Seasons Yield system design, where $SEAS (node) token holders are the owners of the system's yield flow, the capacity to steer the protocol in the right direction should belong to them, as the incentives are aligned with the best progression of the mechanism.
Thus, becoming a DAO member for the Seasons Yield Mechanism is a straightforward process of becoming a node. Every Node (wallet with a qualifying balance above 10,000 $SEAS tokens) is automatically inducted into the DAO and given participation rights.
DAO Power
DAO power is a direct expression of how much influence a member possesses. Power distribution within the Seasons DAO happens pro rata to a member's Node weight on a 1-token-1-unit of power.
The more DAO power a user has, the more votes they have.
Other potential models will be explored, including a time weight factor and a contribution factor.
Proposals
Seasons DAO proposals are independently submitted requests that suggest some kind of operational/technical adaptation to the Yield Mechanism in pursuit of potential improvements.
All DAO members can read and vote on proposals; however, only Nodes above 100,000 $SEAS tokens are given the right to submit a proposal.
Every proposal is submitted with a 250 $SEAS token bond; if a proposal is denied, the bond is removed from circulation. If a proposal is approved, then the bonded $SEAS are returned to the proposer.
Proposals can be in 1 of 4 states:
- Implemented
- Approved
- Denied
- In Revision
- Proposals that are resubmitted incur an additional 50 $SEAS tokens for each resubmission.

The Seasons Partner Program is an initiative to build a network of promoters, recruiters, marketers, salespeople, influencers, and other communication experts who will help expand Seasons' presence, namely the community's OnChain footprint.
Partners help spread the message of Seasons and educate their audiences, friends, and followers about the project's capabilities. They become authorized independent agents endorsed by Seasons and an extension of the project's social growth engine.

chunks.title: Yield 101 › Yield
chunks.text:
A Brief about Yield as we know it.
This is a general reference piece of material to provide a basic level of understanding of Yield. For those seeking a quick orientation with the language, a vocabulary has been provided here.
Yield
Yield is the single most important element of a healthy financial system. It is the foundation upon which the modern economy is built; but what is it?
What is Yield?
At the Highest level, Yield is the value earned/accumulated above the investment cost of an instrument over the course of time. It is a return premium on resources over time allocated to any arbitrary use cases/entities.
Example:
A Government is fundraising from the general public via bonds for telecommunication infrastructure expansions.
Bond face value of a bond is $10,000 (redemption from government) Bonds Mature 10 years after the date they are purchased/"activated". Bonds are Auctioned at $9,000. (discount to their redemption value)
That means the government believes it will be able to complete its task, recoup & profit from the gathered resources within 10 years enough to pay back all investors with a premium as a "thank you" for locking up some of their funds with the government.
In this case, if a person buy a Bond for $9,000 and in 10 years will be able to collect $10,000, their yield is $1,000. In percentage terms, it would be: (Total Profit / Initial investment) ($1,000 / $9,000 ) + 11.11%
That 11.11% is then amortized linearly across 10 years bringing at average APY of 1.11% this example does not take into account variables of buying power or inflation, it is intended for illustrative purposes only.
Yield Before Yield
Civilizations have tapped the power of yield for several millennia as a core essence of social dynamics and ancient economics. The Etymology of the term itself, Yield, comes from Old English & Germanic roots, which translated directly means "to pay, reward/ render, serve". In fact, Yield itself stems from beyond finance as a whole. In the world of agriculture, yield is used by farmers to refer to the harvest of crops they will collect in a given season. In the days of Kings, yield was synonymous with plunder, the spoils of their warfare.
The principle is universal and timeless, profits as it relates to an investment over the course of time.
Yield is Interest is ROI is Rewards.
Which brings us to the days of modern man.

chunks.title: Yield 101 › Yield in The Modern Age
chunks.text:
Yield in The Modern Age
As the information age washed over the world and digitization swallowed society, value has been radically rehypothecated; meanings have lost their origins and almost entirely become reappropriated around money.
Banking has captured the imaginations/fantasy's of society and calibrated Yield entirely into the world of finance. Yield has become a very unsexy subject matter spoken of only in the circles of elites or sovereign nations. Most people remain either unaware or unattracted to the "yields" provided by traditional instrumentation such as government bonds.
If we overly simplify yield into the "cost of money over time"; we find that it exists in two vectors:
- Lending/Borrowing
- Funding Rates
Lending and borrowing is the base foundation of it all, where money that is lent generates yield from the borrower who pays for access to that capital.
Yield in the internet economy remains one of the most elusive elements of finance; before blockchain technology, it was essentially non-existent.
Yield in Web3
Regardless of what narratives may attempt to superimpose into the public's consciousness, blockchain is at its core an autonomous triple-entry accounting system; a DLT divinely perfect transactional record; a financial tool.
Rapidly approaching its second decade in public consciousness, and iterating through many versions, philosophies, and the latest generation of blockchain/DLT ushered in a new era of developmental capabilities through a confluence of social readiness and infrastructural capabilities that have unlocked previously unfathomable logical primitives.
The nascent, early stage of crypto and its countless regulatory hurdles have imposed challenges on the industry which have held it back from fully being able to capture opportunities for yield. Mavericks of open finance have stepped forward with innovative pseudo-reg-tech solutions to push the envelope of creativity, introducing a wholly new class of finance. (including Pendle)
There is a fundamental difference in between crypto-based yield and Real Yield; one is hot air and the other doesn't need crypto to exist.
Yield: Value that is generated (captured/distributed) in a projects native token via inflation or some variation of unbalanced incentives allocation.
Real Yield: Value that is captured/distributed in liquid assets; these tend to have a foundation in the greater world economy such as government T-Bills.
Crypto/DEFI APY's have a muddled, albeit short, history which has made it infamous for unsustainable economic designs. The main culprits are low-fidelity attempts by the builders at arbitrage time through inflationary token models, in which case the teams themselves, or sophisticated market participants, exploit the less-informed populations.
All of the largest, most successful financial institutions, be it a bank, payment processor, hedge fund, centralized exchange, or anything in between, all share two things in common:
1) they obsess about recruiting more customers/clients/users
2) they are built on a business model of transaction fees
They do not care about prices, they do not care about the results of their user's portfolios; what they care about is generating activity; a.k.a. volume.
Yield 3.0
Seasons has identified and leaned into the single most critical element of all yield systems, the focal point around which the global economy is built, and it is not a financial one. That focal point is people; or as the web3 industry loves to call it, community. It then married it with a the same basic transactional fee model and turned the fees outwards, back into the hands of the community (rather than hoarding it).
Seasons is effectively the world's elite's financial system's business model with the logic inverted outward via the open decentralized rails of blockchain technology.
Learn more about: Yield 3.0

chunks.title: Vocabulary › Terminology:
chunks.text:
Terminology:
DEFI - Decentralized Finance
The sector of crypto that deals with financial products. DEFI generally refers to any traditional financial product/instrument that is built on blockchain rails with smart contracts. DEFI also utilizes novel mathematical primitives to unlock new transaction capabilities which in tunr enable a new paradigm of finances otherwise not possible.
Yield
Rate of return on investment: proceeds generated through the allocation of resources over time. For a more comprehensive explanation of Yield please refer to "The State Of Yield" section of this documentation.
Real Yield
Rate of the return on investment; proceeds generated through the allocation of resources over time minus implied expenses, (operational costs), taxes, inflation, and other amortizing elements. For a more comprehensive explanation of Yield please refer to "The State Of Yield" section of this documentation.
APY - Annual Percentage Yield
APY or Annual Percentage Yield is the most common term used to refer to the expected returns on an investment every 365 days. If an investment cost $10,000 and every year it generates $500 in profits without losing value, the APY of that vehicle is 5%.
Node
A focal point, vertex/vector in the topology of a network or diagram at which lines, processes, or pathways intersect. In computer science, nodes can be any arbitrary checkpoint through which information flows, a phone, a computer, switchbox, WIFI router, etc.
QA - Quality Assurance
QA is shorthand for Quality Assurance, the process of ensuring consistency of a product/service through pre-emptive and post-emptive testing. Quality Assurance is quintessential for detecting flaws, reducing errors, and upholding a certain level of expectation or standard.
YR - Yield Rate
The value generated by the Seasons network on a rolling biases. Established through a simple, straight forward formula of (Volume × Value × Transactional Tax).
BC - Blue Chips
A term borrowed from traditional finance, blue chips is used to refer to assets that are generally widely considered to be the most popular, reliable, resilient types of assets within their class/category/industry. Seasons abbreviated the phrase into a two letter acronym to simplify its written articulation (for content as well as code) and reduce its redundancy (for easy of cognitive load). More details available in " Blue Chips " section of this documentation.
UD - Under Dogs
Colloquial term to identify a tier of assets that posses all the markings of a potential tier 1 yet has for some reason not made it yet. The term come from far beyond the financial or crypto worlds, nearly all human endeavors from sports to culinary arts, business, and beyond have an "underdog / under dogs". The easiest way to think of a UD is the 2nd best only because some external force randomly selected the #1. Seasons abbreviated the phrase into a two letter acronym to simplify its written articulation (for content as well as code) and reduce its redundancy (for easy of cognitive load). More details available in " Under Dogs " section of this documentation.
RS - Rising Stars
A tier of early-stage assets with extremely promising potential for tremendous upside in value appreciation, yet possesses equally high risks due to nascency. Seasons abbreviated the phrase into a two-letter acronym to simplify its written articulation (for content as well as code) and reduce its redundancy (for ease of cognitive load). More details available in " Rising Stars " section of this documentation.
HYSA - High Yield Savings Account
HYSA is an acronym for High-Yield Savings account. HYSA's are a common financial instrument in the traditional economy. These tend to be tools for generating passive income with relatively low risk and implications for locking capital. For Seasons, HYSA is a product form factor to succinctly capture one angle of the Yield 3.0 system's implications. More details available in " Under Dogs " section of this documentation.
TTT - Transaction Transfer Tax

chunks.title: Vocabulary › Terminology: (cont.)
chunks.text:
TTT is an acronym for Transaction Transfer Tax; it refers to the revenue model of one of Seasons three yield 3.0 system components. The TTT imposes a fee on every commercial transaction involving an asset ($SEAS token) to generate yield. Every transaction with the $SEAS token, buying, selling, sending, or moving, incurs a 10% cost of the total transaction size. While only the market-based activity contributed to yield generation, the incentive triggers provide a unique gamification angle that aligns with longer-term time preferences. More details available in " TTT " section of this documentation.
SSYM - Stakeholder Stablecoin Yield Module
SSYM is the acronym for Stakeholder Stablecoin Yield Module; one of the three core constituents of its Yield 3.0 system. The SSYM is a pool of stablecoins derived from the yield backlog that fixates yield input-to-output of the system and acts as an interim storage point. While the storage point is awaiting distribution, the assets are put to work in the most risk-minimized way (lending via yield-bearing stablecoin). Proceeds generated while holding are redistributed throughout the network to amplify payout impact and strengthen the bottom line reserves. More details available in " SSYM " section of this documentation.
YAV - Yield Asset Vaults
YAV is the acronym for Yield Asset Vaults; the most technically complex module of the Yield 3.0 system, the YAVs are automated smart contracts that deploy assets into DEFI strategies. Vaults provide unique earning opportunities by encapsulating a wider set of operations with varying risk-reward profiles. Vaults are composed of assets in which Seasons distributes yield and belongs to the $SEAS (node) token holders, accruing proceeds for injection into the network. More details available in " YAV " section of this documentation.
YMS - Yield Management System
The YMS or Yield Management System is an orchestration layer that handles the entire lifecycle of yield in Seasons Yield 3.0 mechanism. The YMS directs and sequences the inputs and outputs between different system components. Coordinating the generation of proceeds with the distribution of them, acting as the oracle to reference the Inclusion and Node sets. More details available in " YMS " section of this documentation.
Epoch
Epoch is a general term used to describe a pre-defined block of time. Many companies, projects, and protocols use Epochs to highlight product or system features. Seasons utilizes the term Epoch to refer to a round of distribution, specifically the total balance of $SEAS tokens on receiving nodes.

chunks.title: High-Yield Savings Account › Node Weights
chunks.text:
Node Weights
The weight of a Node represents its relative claim size as a percentage allocation of the yield distribution, determining the portion attributable to it at that distribution event. A Node's weight can, will, and usually does fluctuate from distribution event to distribution event.
Weight is determined by:
1. Adding together the $SEAS token balances of all active nodes
2. Dividing any individual node's balance by the aggregate sum
This ratio establishes the relative proportions of a distribution. The larger the weight, the larger the portion of a distribution.
The passive management, pay-to-play configuration, and risk profile of a node in the portfolio of an operator position the node as a HYSA (High Yield Savings Account).
Membership
- In the future, DAO membership shall be granted exclusively to NODEs.
FAQs - HYSA
Q: What does HYSA mean??
A: HYSA is the acronym that stands for High-Yield Savings Account.
Q: How much does a HYSA generate?
A: It varies on a per-payout basis, currently targeting ~>12% APY.
Q: What is the TTT Rate?
A: The current tax rate for a transaction is 10%.
Q: Can the TTT Rate change?
A: Yes. The rate can be adjusted to anything the SEASON Node Network deems to be ideal. Adaptation of the rate becomes a consideration after the instantiation of the DAO.
Q: Are all transactions subject to TTT?
A: Yes, every action involving the movement of $SEAS tokens from point A to point B triggers the TTT, including swaps (buy/sell), transfers (send/receive), and all smart contract invocation (escrow, provide LP, or locking).
Q: What happens with fees accumulated during transfers?
A: Whenever $SEAS tokens are taxed on a transfer, they do not generate fees. Having no economic significance to the network, those tokens are recycled through the YMS (Yield Management System).
Q: What is the potential APY of a node?
A: Subjective and circumstantial; the APY of a node is determined by a multitude of factors acting in orchestration with each other. Seasons aims to achieve consistency within its target range of 6.58%-21.07%; however, variance outside of it is to be expected.
Q: Should I split my Node if it has over 10,000 tokens?
It is a matter of preference and wallet management. All nodes are treated equally. Whether it is one address with 20,000 tokens or 2 addresses with 10,000 tokens each, they will generate equally proportional yield.
Q: Will the requirement ever change?
Potentially by community consensus only after the DAO has been fully integrated.
Q: Can I sell my tokens and still generate yield?
Yes, so long as the balance of your wallet is above 10,000 $SEAS, you will continue generating yield.
Q: What assets do NODEs generate?
That depends on the "Inclusion List" at the time of acquisition/distribution.

About Seasons
Seasons is an autonomous on-chain yield protocol making real-asset returns accessible to anyone with a Solana wallet — no banks, no intermediaries, no minimum wealth requirements.
Real yield, for everyone
Our mission
Real yield, for everyone
The financial system has always distributed the best yields to those who need them least. Wealthy institutions access yield-generating assets — gold, bonds, real estate — that ordinary savers cannot. Seasons changes this. By building yield distribution directly into a token's economics, anyone who holds $SEAS earns real-asset returns twice a week, automatically. No relationship manager required. No minimum account size. No paperwork.
Autonomous by design
How we build
Autonomous by design
The Seasons protocol is designed to operate without human intervention. TTT fees are collected on-chain by the SPL-2022 token standard. The Yield Management System (YMS) converts them to the Inclusion Set assets automatically. Distribution to node wallets happens on-chain, on schedule, without anyone pressing a button. The team's role is to set parameters, evolve the system, and eventually hand control to the DAO.
